parameters.content:
## I.LPRA — LP report 134 "Jobs by Milestone Date" (thin transport ONLY)

Gmail → keep every **`.csv`** attachment → POST the CSV **text** → LP-MCP.
ZERO parsing here: every parse / validate / write rule lives in LP-MCP (fail-closed).
LP schedules this email ~6:00 ET daily · scope **MTD + prior month through business day 5** · feeds Net — Released and `revenue_as_of`.

**⚠️ THE SIX-DAY SILENT OUTAGE (2026-08-06 → 2026-08-12).** LP switched from the
Report Scheduler to the Export Scheduler: PDF `mrichard5152_134_..._Jobs by
Milestone Date.pdf` became CSV `_260812030038_Export.csv`. The report id left the
filename, so the `_134_` test matched nothing, the Code node emitted zero items,
and the POST never ran. **Zero items is not an error**, so the run went green in
29ms and the failure telemetry — which only fires on a POST response — never
fired. `revenue_as_of` froze at 2026-08-06 while the dashboard read "success".
The four sibling workflows were migrated to CSV on 2026-08-10; this one was
missed, which is why 134 alone went stale.

**Routing is by HEADER, not filename.** LP's CSV attachments are named
`_<YYMMDDHHMMSS>_Export.csv` and carry no report id. LP-MCP's
`detectReportFromHeader` fingerprints the file; the slug in the URL is only a
hint. Scope comes from the Gmail subject query.

**The body is raw TEXT, not binary.** n8n's binary body mode sends multipart and
overrides Content-Type, which the route rejects with 400 "POST the CSV text as
the request body". The Code node decodes to `json.csv_text`; the HTTP node posts
it raw as `text/csv`.

**⚠️ The trigger needs `downloadAttachments: true` and the `attachment_` prefix.**
Without them the trigger returns messages with NO binary, the Code node has
nothing to loop over, and it emits zero items — the same silent shape as above.

**Node names still say "PDF".** Deliberate, matching I.LPRB–F: `connections`
reference nodes by name. The wire is CSV.

**Failure handling.** 200 + `success:false` = deterministic rejection — never
retried; logged in `scorecard_ingest_log` + GroupMe. 5xx = transport error —
retried 3×, then reported to `/events/lp_report_ingest_failed`.

**Both outcomes now report (2026-08-29).** The IF's FALSE branch goes to
`/events/lp_report_ingest_failed`; its TRUE branch goes to
`/events/lp_report_ingest_succeeded`. TRUE used to dead-end, so a SUCCESSFUL 134
ingest emitted no event at all — the same blind spot that let report 133 read as
broken for eight days after it was fixed.

**⚠️ IT STILL WILL NOT CATCH THE OUTAGE DESCRIBED ABOVE.** Both telemetry
branches hang off the POST's response, and the six-day failure was the POST
never firing at all. A zero-item run reaches neither branch and stays silent.
The guard against THAT is a freshness check on `revenue_as_of`, not this.

**⚠️ This telemetry row shares a report_type with the parser.** `jobs-by-milestone`
maps to `jobs_by_milestone` on BOTH sides, so every successful run writes TWO
rows to `scorecard_ingest_log`. Tell them apart by `source` (`n8n_telemetry` vs
`n8n`) and by `snapshot_id`, which is null on the telemetry row. Any query
counting successes MUST filter on `source` or it will double-count.
